caption: The drawing is divided into two main sections, an upper and lower half, each containing a series of stylized figures and shapes created with a stippled or dotted background. In the upper left quadrant, there is a reddish-brown humanoid figure on a dark textured background, with an elongated body featuring a lattice pattern, four-fingered hands, and feet, and head branches or antlers extending upward and outward. The upper right quadrant, set against a tan stippled background, contains a reddish-brown creature with a vertically ribbed, elongated body, similar four-fingered hands and feet, round circular forms at the elbows, and radiating lines or spikes along the body and head. The lower half, also set against a tan background, includes four forms: In the upper left, a red zigzag line; below it, a small reddish-brown humanoid figure with many spikes or lines radiating from its head and back. In the center, another reddish humanoid figure with a patterned body and bifurcated antler-like branches extending from the head, and spiral lines forming the arms. On the right side, a solid black humanoid figure with a blocky body and head topped with vertical lines or spikes, and hands and feet with prominent fingers and toes. The composition emphasizes earthy tones of red, rust, black, and tan, with simple lines and patterns.
title: Petroglyph
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
